questions.q: Which strategy trains one model for each horizon step?
why: MIMO has one model with many outputs.

questions.q: A recursive forecast uses the lag y(t-1) at step 3. What value should it use?
options: The real value if it is in the test data
The model's own prediction for that time
why: In real use the future is unknown. Using it is a leak.
Correct: predictions are fed back into the history.

questions.q: You need a horizon of 24 steps with a direct strategy. How many models do you train for one series?
Select all true statements about the recursive strategy.
options: It needs only one trained model
It needs one model per horizon step
Unknown future covariates are a problem
why: Yes: predictions with errors become inputs.
No. That is the direct strategy.
Yes: each step needs covariate values, so they must be known or forecast too.

questions.q: Your gradient boosting model must forecast 90 days. Training 90 direct models is too slow. Which options are reasonable?
options: Use recursion and check the error growth by step
Use a global model with the step number as a feature, or block models
Both are reasonable options to compare
why: Reasonable, but not the only one.
Reasonable, but not the only one.
Correct: compare cheap options in a backtest and keep the best one.

questions.q: A direct model for step k = 10 is trained on a series of 100 points with window 10. How many rows does it have?
Why can a direct strategy produce a 'jumpy' forecast path?
options: Each step model is trained separately, so neighbouring steps are not forced to be consistent
why: Correct: nothing links the models of step 3 and step 4.
Direct models use only the information at the origin.
The window length is not the cause.
